reasons: The Controller-bound record shows the required stratified search sequence was executed: complementary recent authoritative reviews established the map and taxonomy, high-citation work supplied the historical and mechanistic backbone, recent elite-venue work covered current methods and hotspots, and targeted follow-up addressed identified gaps.

Coverage is decision-grade rather than artifact-only: the bound Corpus and Ledger retain screening, admission, and retrieval decisions; 99 full-text/read events support 82 accepted Evidence Cards; and all 19 continuation records previously lacking canonical Evidence were reviewed and submitted. No unsupported abstract-only frontier dependency is reported.

The Field Map covers the principal scientific bottlenecks and method boundaries across mechanical-port realization, transition control, uncertainty, compliant actuation, variable-gain energy management, learning and reinforcement learning, predictive constraints, human adaptation, physical-prior compensation, and deployment assurance.

The nine declared development traces provide evidence-card-supported causal explanations for methodological evolution, including parallel branches and a cross-family safety reframing, without inferring transitions from chronology or citation order alone.

The unresolved leads are appropriately framed as frontier problem-generation directions rather than demonstrated missing top-level branches, and none presently changes the field-evolution explanation, method boundary, dominant bottlenecks, or frontier judgment.

foundation_to_frontier.rationale: The map connects the foundational mechanical-port impedance, admittance, and passivity vocabulary to implementation-aware realization, robust and adaptive control, variable-energy management, learned and energy-structured methods, constrained predictive control, hierarchical skills, and intent-adaptive interaction. It also identifies the residual frontier in sampled-solver feasibility, layered assurance, distribution shift, transfer, complex contact, objective selection, and human evidence.

key_nodes_and_branches.rationale: The twelve method families and nine bottleneck classes capture the major nodes, parallel branches, forks, and continuing coexistence of classical realization, contact-transition, robust/adaptive, compliant-actuation, learning, passivity-management, reinforcement-learning, energy-structured, online-optimization, predictive-safety, human-adaptive, and physics-prior approaches. The map does not force these into a single replacement sequence.

transition_causality.rationale: All nine declared traces identify a motivating limitation, the subsequent methodological response, and the residual bottleneck. Their causal bases include realized-port mismatch, energy injection from variable gains, uncertainty and distribution shift, task-specific transfer limits, sequencing needs, explicit constraint requirements, response-time demands, human-intent uncertainty, and the need to separate safety properties; these are substantive mechanisms rather than chronological inference.

explanatory_coherence.rationale: The map explains why the field developed into its current form: interaction-relation realization exposed hardware and uncertainty limits; adaptation and learning improved performance but created energetic, transfer, and certificate mismatches; predictive and property-specific assurance addressed explicit constraints while exposing discretization, feasibility, fallback, and deployment gaps. The current frontier is therefore coherently located at the integration of performance adaptation with implementation-aware, layered, failure-inclusive assurance in complex human and multi-contact settings.
